recipes.name: Chicken Breasts Supreme
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup
1 (4.5 ounce) can sliced mushrooms, drained and chopped
0.5 cup processed cheese (such as Velveeta®), diced

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 2-quart casserole dish.

Season chicken breasts with salt, pepper, and paprika. Melt butter in a large skillet; add chicken and brown well on both sides, about 5 minutes per side. Transfer chicken to the prepared casserole dish.

Combine mushroom soup, mushrooms, processed cheese, milk, onion, and Worcestershire sauce in a saucepan over medium-low heat until cheese melts, but do not boil. Stir to thoroughly combine, then stir in sour cream until smooth. Pour sauce over chicken; cover with foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until chicken tender and juices run clear, about 45 minutes. Uncover dish, baste with sauce; continue baking 30 minutes more, basting occasionally.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Breasts Supreme
raw_recipe.description: Chicken breasts are browned and coated and baked in a creamy, cheesy sauce with mushrooms for a family-pleasing main dish.

review.reviewBody: This was easy and delicious! I substituted grated cheddar cheese for the processed cheese.

This was a great recipe base, but I changed a few things. These are chicken breasts, so they shouldn't need to be baked that long to cook thoroughly. I will reduce the baking time next time. I used fresh mushrooms and real cheese. I precooked the onions and mushrooms and added some garlic then added the soup and the rest of the ingredients...yum! The sauce is delish. I made noodles to accompany the chicken...the family loved it!

This is great! I did use a few variations, based on what I had in my kitchen. I think it's ok to vary a recipe, especially if you have to and it's great to read reviews about them, so you are more confident in your own ability to do so. I don't ever have canned mushrooms in the house, so after browning the chicken, I put that in the casserole and then sauteed 8 oz. of fresh baby bellas until they cooked down pretty well. Instead of 1/3 C. of milk, I used an entire soup can, based on wanting some extra sauce, and I used whole yogurt instead of sour cream, which I prefer. I might add some fresh crushed garlic to the mushroom saute next time. Everyone loved it. It really was delicious and we will make this again. I was looking for something to stretch 14 oz. of chicken for a family of four and this worked well! Thank you!

This was delicious. I thought the Worcestershire sauce would be too much but it mellowed out in the baking. I split 4 very large boneless chicken breasts so there were 8 6-oz servings. I would double the sauce amount the next time because there wasn't too much left for the leftover chicken. I served it with egg noodles but there wasn't enough sauce left to serve with sauced noodles again, I'll just make buttered noodles for a side. I don't use canned mushrooms and I was too lazy to slice what I had so I didn't add them. This would make a great sauce for beef too. I also wouldn't cook for so long as the chicken was nearly cooked in the browning stage. I would bake for 1/2 hr covered and 15 minutes uncovered.

Great and easy. I used fresh mushrooms and shredded cheddar cheese instead of the processed cheese, and it came out great. Sautéed the mushrooms and onions in a bit of butter dirt in the saucepan, then added everything else to it. I used thinner chicken breasts so only had to put it in the oven for about 20 mins. But great easy weeknight dish to jazz up your chicken.

Made some changes on the fly. Recipe is way too much cooking. Butterfly chicken, season with lemon pepper, smoked paprika, salt. Pan with butter only 3 minutes per side to brown. No milk on hand so used half half. Extra tablespoon of minced onion, extra tablespoon of Worcestershire. Traded processed cheese for grated pepper jack, grated extra sharp white cheddar and a lil grated Parmesan…. Baked only 20 minutes then off and leave in oven while preparing table and plating pasta. Winner winner chicken dinner!

Only me to cook for so I used only 1 chicken breast and halved the sauce recipe. I also used grated cheddar rather than Velveeta and cut the cooking time - 30 minutes covered; 20 minutes uncovered. Served with pasta and green salad. This was absolutely delicious! I still have sauce left for another meal as well. Definitely a keeper!

Amazing! We did not need 6 breasts as it is only two of us. We used 3 breasts and doubled the sauce. (We made a pot of rice for the side and the extra sauce made an excellent "gravy")
We used real cheese instead of processed and it was splendid! We also added Broccoli when we added the sour cream and that was just awesome! Due to the smaller amount of chicken we reduced the cooking time and the first round with foil went for 30 minutes and then when the foil was removed it was done and at temperature in another 25 minutes.

Made per the recipe except for the cook time and cheese. Used freshly grated cheddar and sliced breasts in half to thin them a bit so only needed 20 minutes covered and 20 uncovered. Family named this new favorite Chicken Stroganoff . Yum!

This was great are used for fat pieces of chicken are used about a quarter cup of Sweet onions which I sautéed with fresh baby portobello.Kept everything else exactly the same it came out spectacular it’s definitely a prize winning Dish.We loved it and there’s two pieces for tomorrow.
This was delicious! I used real cheddar cheese instead of velveeta. I also doubled the sauce, as I used two casserole dishes. A great addition to recipe collection. Thank you

Really good blend of flavors. I used Cream of Chicken soup instead. Can't improve on this much other than to use fresh mushrooms if you have them, and DO NOT cook as long as the directions say. I checked at the 30 minute mark and the chicken was done. I took off the foil, put it back in the oven for maybe another 15 minutes while prepping side dishes, and it was perfect!
Really easy and made adjustments per our tastes. My husband doesn't like sour cream, left that out, used Blanco and mozzarella cheese with the cream of mushroom soup and served with pasta. Wonderful.
I added 1/4 cup heavy whipping cream, green onions, and minced garlic to the mix for a little more flavor. served over linguine.
Instead I grated some Balderson Old Cheddar on the sauce. Thank you for the recipe.
Not our fav bec of very creamy sauce.
First time making it. Cubed the chicken breast and used portobello mushrooms. Was very good, and easy to put together. Good flavor
Great & easy shredded cheese instead of processed fresh mushrooms in stead of canned

I miss the Allrecipes option to adjust for servings. Cooking for two after a family of six is a challenge. I only used one chicken breast but these days they are the size of a turkey breast. As others have noted, I don't ever use processed cheese and so used a combo of mozzarella, cheddar with the sour cream and cream of chicken with herbs soup. I reduced ingredients to half and it worked great for two people. Served over egg noodles with fresh green beans.
